business.text: A pre-order website for a small bakery that lets regular customers reserve their usual bread so it's held for them.

positioning.text: Gives a small bakery the same online ordering that bigger chains have, making it easier for loyal customers to get what they want.

customers.text: Regular morning customers who come every day and are frustrated when their preferred bread, especially the sourdough, sells out by nine.

whatSells.text: The guarantee that their usual loaf will be waiting for them, no matter what time they arrive.

brandFeel.text: As personal as the baker who already knows you—don't ask what you already know.

strengths.text: She excels at customer conversations and translating what she hears into product decisions.

waysOfWorking.text: She prefers to stay close to customers and use their feedback to guide what gets built.

philosophy.believe: We build first for the regulars who come in every morning and lose out when the sourdough is gone by nine.
philosophy.guidance: Design the first version around a regular reserving their usual loaf, sourdough above all, so it's held for them at pickup. Recruit a few morning regulars to test it before adding anything for other customers.

philosophy.believe: For a regular, ordering should feel like being recognized at the counter: the bakery already knows you, so the site should too.
philosophy.guidance: Never ask a regular for anything we already know, like their name, their usual loaf or their usual pickup time. Make the 'Reserve usual loaf' path start pre-filled so it's a single confirm, not a form.
